dropped.note: REJECT — THE PROPOSAL WOULD REPLACE A CORRECT, AUTHORITY-SANCTIONED FORM, AND ITS CENTRAL FACTUAL CLAIM IS FALSE. The proposal asserts SAOL 'does NOT list *keyboards' and concludes the stored 'Keyboards' is a script artifact to be replaced by 'Keyboardar'. It consulted SAOL only. I fetched BOTH authorities and re-verified twice: SO reads 'keyboard keyboarden el. keyboardet, plural KEYBOARDS äv. keyboardar' — SO lists KEYBOARDS FIRST, as its primary plural. So the stored value is not invented and is not wrong; it is SO's first-listed form, and the proposal's own first-listed policy (which it invokes by name: 'Taking SAOL's first-listed form') would endorse it under SO. What is actually here is the brief's rule-5 class exactly: SAOL ('pl. ~ar el. ~' — keyboardar or zero, no -s) and SO ('keyboards äv. keyboardar') GENUINELY DISAGREE, like bison/mango/frisbee. Per the brief that is 'a finding to FLAG, not something to resolve by picking' — and the proposal picked, silently, without disclosing that the other authority contradicts it. Destroying a correct form is the worst outcome available here. LEAVE 'Keyboards' STANDING and surface the SAOL/SO conflict to the operator. (Note the row's gender 't' is also sanctioned — SAOL '~en el. ~et' — so no consequential change follows.)

escalated.note: THE FIX IS DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT BUT MUST NOT SHIP AS WRITTEN — my rule-7 dup scan caught the one thing the first round did not. 'Sjukhuskläderar' is indefensible (the -ar default bolted onto an already-plural noun; SAOB: 'KLÄDER, pl., se KLÄDE'), so it cannot stay. But patching the plural to 'Sjukhuskläder' makes this row ['Sjukhuskläder','Sjukhuskläder','n'] BYTE-IDENTICAL to the sister key 'scrubs' — the ONLY new collision my scan found across all 39 patched keys, and one CREATED by the fix rather than pre-existing. The two keys are different garments: scrubs is what STAFF wear (de OP-Kleidung, es Uniforme médico, nl Operatiekleding) and a hospital gown is what the PATIENT wears. The cross-locale test makes this decisive: ALL 10 other locales give hospital-gown a COUNTABLE singular patient garment with a real plural (de Krankenhaushemd/Krankenhaushemden, fr Blouse d'hôpital/Blouses d'hôpital, es Bata de hospital/Batas, it Camice ospedaliero/Camici, nl Ziekenhuisjas/Ziekenhuisjassen, da Hospitalskittel/Hospitalskitler, no Sykehuskjole/Sykehuskjoler, fi Sairaalatakki/Sairaalatakit) — Swedish ALONE has collapsed a patient gown into plural-only 'hospital clothes', which is precisely why the script had nothing to pluralise. AND the proposal's stated ground is false: 'Removing the invented form is right whichever way the lemma question is settled' does NOT hold — if the lemma resolves to Patientrock the plural is Patientrockar, not Sjukhuskläder, so this fix is not lemma-independent and would entrench the defect behind a duplicate. Operator must rule the lemma (recommend Patientrock/Patientrockar/n, which also resolves the separately-held gender row, since a plural-only noun can carry neither en nor ett). Delete the non-word — but do not ship a byte-identical twin of scrubs.

NO PLURAL IS ATTESTED ANYWHERE, AND THE PROPOSAL'S ANALOGUE IS THE WRONG CLASS. Verified verbatim: 'Inga träffar på iguanodon' in SAOL, SO and SAOB alike — quoted honestly by the proposal. I then went one step further and checked the source the proposal did not cite: sv.wiktionary DOES have an iguanodon entry, but it carries only 'iguanodon u' with NO Böjningar table at all — so the gender (utrum, = the stored n) is corroborated while the plural is attested by nothing, in any source. That leaves the proposed 'Iguanodoner' resting entirely on the cited elektron pattern — and that analogue does not hold: elektron/proton/neutron are -tron/-on words, whereas iguanodon is a Greek -ODON word (sv.wiktionary etymology: 'grekiska ὀδών (odṓn)'). SAOL's actual -odon control is 'mast·odont [-odån´t] substantiv ~en ~er' — Swedish nativises Greek -odon by taking the oblique stem odont- and adding a -T, giving mastodont -> mastodonter. That points at a LEMMA question (Iguanodont -> iguanodonter?), which per the brief is reserved to the operator and is more than a form correction. Both the stored -ar (the script's unmotivated default; the Latin -us rule cannot reach a Greek stem) and the proposed -er are unattested guesses, so this is not 'keep the stored value' — it is 'neither form is sourced; rule it explicitly'. The proposal itself invites exactly this ('Operator may prefer to leave it pending a native/palaeontology-usage check'), and I agree: do not ship an invented plural to children on a pattern argument built from the wrong word class.
